cues.en: Without long distance communication,
cues.zh: 如果没有远程通信，

cues.en: the modern world would not function as it does. That's obvious.
cues.zh: 现代世界就无法像现在这样运转，显而易见。

cues.en: Take this equipment for instance. It's a receiving system in contact with a navigational satellite 600 miles up, circling the earth north south,
cues.zh: 就拿这台设备来说，它是一个接收系统，正与 600 英里高空沿南北方向绕地球运行的导航卫星通信，

cues.en: so that as the earth turns beneath it, the satellite covers the entire globe.
cues.zh: 随着地球在它下方自转，这颗卫星便能覆盖整个地球。

cues.en: Now, as it comes over, it broadcasts two things. It says where it is, and it sends out a continuous note at a very precise frequency.
cues.zh: 当它飞过上空时，会广播两样东西：当前所在的位置，以及一个频率极精准的连续音调。

cues.en: Now, if you compare that note to the sound, say, of the whistle of a train, as the train comes towards you and goes away, the note rises and then falls like this.
cues.zh: 如果你把这个音调比作火车的汽笛声，当火车朝你驶来又离去时，音调会先升高后降低，就像这样。

cues.en: Now, the way the note rises or falls depends on where you hear it from.
cues.zh: 而音调升降的方式，完全取决于你所处的位置。

cues.en: If you knew exactly where the train was,
cues.zh: 如果你确切知道火车的位置，

cues.en: then what you were listening to would tell you where you were because you'd only hear it that way in that place.
cues.zh: 那么听到的声音就能告诉你自己在哪里，因为只有在那个特定的地点，你听到的声音才会是那样的。

cues.en: And that's what this equipment does.
cues.zh: 这正是这台设备的作用。

cues.en: There's the receiver locking into the signal from the satellite.
cues.zh: 接收器正在锁定来自卫星的信号。

cues.en: Now, the computer is working out the one location on Earth, where a satellite at that particular point in space would give it the noise it's hearing.
cues.zh: 现在，计算机正在推算地球上唯一的这个位置——在这个位置上，处于太空中特定点的卫星才会产生它所接收到的这种信号。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好了。

cues.en: Here's where we are.
cues.zh: 这就是我们所在的位置。

cues.en: North,
cues.zh: 北纬，

cues.en: forty three degrees, forty two minutes, twelve point one seconds.
East,
cues.zh: 东经，

cues.en: four degrees, forty three minutes, eighteen point eight seconds.
Right, you check those numbers out on a map, and this is where it says we are. South Of France,
cues.zh: 没错，在地图上查一下这些坐标，这里就是它指示的位置：法国南部，

cues.en: near the town of Arles,
cues.zh: 阿尔勒镇附近，

cues.en: at a position accurate
cues.zh: 位置精度

cues.en: to within 30 feet, precisely there,
cues.zh: 在 30 英尺以内，正是那里，

cues.en: where it says there is an ancient aqueduct.
cues.zh: 地图上标着有一座古引水道的地方。

cues.en: There it is.
cues.zh: 就在那儿。

cues.en: Telecommunications
cues.zh: 电信技术

cues.en: can pinpoint somebody, like that did.
cues.zh: 能像这样精准定位一个人。

cues.en: Or because he picks up a telephone,
cues.zh: 或者仅仅因为他拿起电话，

cues.en: because he's on a computer data bank.
cues.zh: 因为他记录在计算机数据库中。

cues.en: We organize ourselves better because of that.
cues.zh: 我们也因此组织得更加高效。

cues.en: The question is,
cues.zh: 但问题是，

cues.en: how well organized will we become?
cues.zh: 我们会被组织到何种程度？

cues.en: Too well?
cues.zh: 过于严密吗？

cues.en: To a certain extent, the modern world would fall apart
cues.zh: 在某种程度上，现代世界会分崩离析，

cues.en: without that organizational ability.
cues.zh: 要是没有那种组织能力的话。

cues.en: The new community of nations that has grown up from the bits and pieces of the old European empires, the French, the English, the Dutch, the Spanish, Portuguese,
cues.zh: 从法国、英国、荷兰、西班牙、葡萄牙等旧欧洲帝国的废墟中崛起的新国家共同体，

cues.en: is held together because we can organize.
cues.zh: 之所以能凝聚在一起，正是因为我们具备组织能力。

cues.en: But what will that organizational network, that communications network,
cues.zh: 但这种组织网络、这种通信网络，

cues.en: do to us next?
cues.zh: 接下来又会对我们产生什么影响？

cues.en: Well, the answer to that question may lie in the past, because this kind of situation's happened before.
cues.zh: 这个问题的答案或许就在过去，因为类似的情况以前就发生过。

cues.en: The last time a world empire fell apart was about fifteen hundred years ago.
cues.zh: 上一次世界性帝国崩溃，大约是在一千五百年前。

cues.en: Then, the empire was Roman.
cues.zh: 当时那个帝国，就是罗马帝国。

cues.en: Now this is the accepted view of the fall of Rome, you know, rape and village, destruction the way Hollywood does it. But what really let the barbarians walk all over the Romans was something it won't take you a second to sympathize with. The taxes were too high to pay for the army that was losing all the battles and a bunch of freeloaders in government, and of course, to pay for thousands of civil servants.
cues.zh: 关于罗马沦陷，大家普遍认同的景象就像好莱坞拍的那样：烧杀劫掠、彻底摧毁。但真正让蛮族肆意践踏罗马人的原因，你一听就能感同身受：税负实在太重了，既要供养屡战屡败的军队和政府里的一大批闲散寄生虫，当然，还要养活成千上万的公务员。

cues.en: So for the Western Romans,
cues.zh: 所以对西罗马人来说，

cues.en: better the barbarian you didn't know than the tax collector you did. So the place fell apart.
cues.zh: 不认识的蛮族，也比认识的税吏强。于是那个地方就分崩离析了。

cues.en: The imperial provinces
cues.zh: 帝国行省

cues.en: cracked up into small barbarian kingdoms.
cues.zh: 分裂成一个个小蛮族王国。

cues.en: And all that big time stuff you have to have with imperial government, you know, super highways, theaters, aqueducts, were no longer worth the upkeep.
cues.zh: 而帝国政府非得配的那些大工程——公路、剧场、引水渠——已经不值得维护了。

cues.en: That's why we're here outside Arles. This aqueduct fed the biggest industrial complex in Europe with water to run the wheels of the great grain mills at Barbagall.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么我们来到阿尔勒城外。这条引水渠为欧洲最大的工业综合体供水，驱动 Barbagall 大型谷物磨坊的水轮。

cues.en: 28 tons of flour a day, a technological marvel perhaps to be lost forever in the chaos.
cues.zh: 一天28吨面粉，这项技术奇迹也许会在混乱中永远失传。

cues.en: All through this period, the so called dark ages, the one organization that still functioned internationally,
cues.zh: 在整个这一时期，也就是所谓的黑暗时代，有一个组织仍在国际层面运作，

cues.en: still traveled the Roman roads when nobody else would, handling the king's local and foreign affairs because its members could still read and write, was the church.
cues.zh: 别人都不走的时候，它仍走罗马大道，处理国王的本地和外交事务，因为其成员还能读写——那就是教会。

cues.en: It had a fully operational network of communications from bishop to bishop throughout Europe, and that's what held things together.
cues.zh: 它有一套覆盖欧洲、主教之间全面运转的通信网络，正是它把一切维系在一起。

cues.en: The church then
cues.zh: 那时的教会

cues.en: was like our telecommunications
cues.zh: 就像我们的电信系统

cues.en: now.
cues.zh: 今天。

cues.en: And so the knowledge that the monks had accumulated gradually spread,
cues.zh: 于是修士们积累的知识逐渐传播开来，

cues.en: knowledge like how Barbagall had worked with the great water wheel and the gearing system that made it so efficient.
cues.zh: 比如 Barbagall 如何运用巨大的水轮，以及让它如此高效的齿轮系统。

cues.en: And in the end, by the Middle Ages,
cues.zh: 最终，到中世纪时，

cues.en: look what they did with that wheel.
cues.zh: 看看他们用那个轮子做出了什么。

cues.en: Here's the wheel being operated by water, and here's the gearing system turning the horizontal movement vertical,
cues.zh: 这里是水力驱动的水轮，这里是齿轮系统把水平运动转为垂直运动，

cues.en: then horizontal again, and then vertical again in order to operate the millstones.
cues.zh: 然后再转回水平，再转成垂直，用来驱动磨石。

cues.en: Here's another system operating a trip hammer for bashing things like mineral ore or cloth or leather, soften it up. Here's a system that operates a similar trip hammer device, but it's to work a suction pump for a water supply.
cues.zh: 这是另一套系统，带动锻锤，用来捶打矿石、布料或皮革之类的东西，把它们弄软。这套系统带动类似的锻锤装置，但用来驱动供水抽水泵。

cues.en: Same system again operating two levers, pressing on bellows for a blast furnace.
cues.zh: 还是同一套系统，带动两个杠杆，挤压高炉的风箱。

cues.en: And finally, over here, a crank that turns a circular movement into back and forward movement for a sawmill.
cues.zh: 最后，在这边，一个曲柄把圆周运动变成往复运动，用于锯木厂。

cues.en: Beautiful system.
cues.zh: 精妙的系统。

cues.en: So put yourself in their position. The wars are all over. There's loads of productive land everywhere. You've got water coming out of your ears and an amazing machine to use to harness the power.
cues.zh: 所以设身处地想一想。战争都结束了。到处都有大量可耕种的土地。水多到用不完，还有神奇的机器能驾驭这股力量。

cues.en: What would you do?
cues.zh: 你会怎么办？

cues.en: Yes.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: You'd have yourself a medieval industrial revolution.
cues.zh: 你会搞出一场中世纪工业革命。

cues.en: The great thing about these wheels was that they were easy to make, and they'd work almost anywhere.
cues.zh: 这些水轮的好处是容易制造，而且几乎在任何地方都能用。

cues.en: You lived up a mountain, hollow a few trees out, and you had yourself a wooden aqueduct.
cues.zh: 你住在山上，就把几棵树掏空，便有了自己的木质引水渠。

cues.en: Horizontal wheels didn't need gears because they spun millstones directly above.
cues.zh: 卧式水轮不需要齿轮，因为它直接在正上方驱动磨石。

cues.en: You could turn a vertical wheel with water falling from above or flowing past below in a river.
cues.zh: 你可以让水从上方落下，或让河水从下方流过，来转动立式水轮。

cues.en: And with gears, you could slow down the effect of a fast stream or speed up a slow one.
cues.zh: 有了齿轮，就能让快的水流变慢，让慢的水流变快。

cues.en: Water power made you a lot of bread in both senses.
cues.zh: 水力让你在两种意义上都赚了很多面包——面包和钱。

cues.en: But the star of the show was this, the
cues.zh: 但好戏的主角是这个——

cues.en: With a cam, you can trick hammers to pound things with, harder and faster than any human being.
cues.zh: 用凸轮，你能让锤子以超过任何人的力量和速度砸东西。

cues.en: And build yourself mills to work, timber, oil, grain, leather, cloth, iron, beer, wire, sugar, coin,
cues.zh: 给自己建磨坊，用来加工木材、油、谷物、皮革、布料、铁、啤酒、金属丝、糖、钱币，

cues.en: you name
cues.zh: 你能想到的，

cues.en: It took a lot of energetic monks to get it all together.
cues.zh: 需要很多精力充沛的修士才能把这些整合起来。

cues.en: Now, they were energetic because in 1098,
cues.zh: 他们精力充沛，是因为在1098年，

cues.en: a bunch of Benedictines,
cues.zh: 一群本笃会修士，

cues.en: fed up with the luxury and the ritual, lit out for the wild country and the simple life, and Saint Benedict's original idea that hard work was good for the soul.
cues.zh: 他们受够了奢华和仪式，奔向荒野和简朴生活，并回归圣本笃最初的理念：辛勤劳动有益于灵魂。

cues.en: But it was the way these Cistercians organized themselves
cues.zh: 但正是这些西多会修士的组织方式

cues.en: that turned them into a medieval multinational
cues.zh: 把他们变成了一个中世纪的跨国企业

cues.en: and gave Europe systems management.
cues.zh: 并给欧洲带来了系统管理。

cues.en: See, each monastery had to be self sufficient in food, so they cut back on the praying and added six hours labor a day. They went into rearing animals, clearing and draining land,
cues.zh: 你看，每座修道院都必须在食物上自给自足，所以他们减少祈祷，每天增加六小时劳动。他们开始饲养动物、开垦和排干土地，

cues.en: they went out looking for new plants they could grow, They wrote each other reports on the latest developments.
cues.zh: 他们外出寻找可以种植的新植物，还互相写报告汇报最新进展。

cues.en: Like this one, growing vines on bad land, hillside terraces.
cues.zh: 比如这一份：在贫瘠土地上种葡萄藤，修山坡梯田。

cues.en: They used all the technology
cues.zh: 他们用上了所有技术

cues.en: wine presses, water mills, iron foundries.
cues.zh: 压酒机、水磨、铸铁厂。

cues.en: A Cistercian Abbey was like a corporation
cues.zh: 一座西多会修道院就像一家公司

cues.en: with the special advantage that at the end of a hard day's business, they served the house wine in the company canteen.
cues.zh: 特殊优势是，忙碌一天的业务结束后，他们会在公司食堂供应自酿葡萄酒。

cues.en: Mind you, the food wasn't that hot. No meat, they sold all that. Just vegetables,
cues.zh: 不过，伙食不怎么样。没有肉，肉都卖了。只有蔬菜，

cues.en: nettle soup, a few roots, bread, and silence
cues.zh: 荨麻汤、几根根茎、面包，还有沉默

cues.en: while you listen to instructive selections from the corporation handbook on getting spiritual and managerial strategy right, otherwise known as the rule of Saint Benedict.
cues.zh: 一边听着公司手册的教诲选段，讲如何把精神和管理策略搞对，也就是所谓的《圣本笃会规》。

cues.en: Well, with this kind of organization, how could you fail? Within a century, there were nearly 600 Cistercian monasteries.
cues.zh: 有了这种组织，怎么会失败？一个世纪内，就有了近600座西多会修道院。

cues.en: These monks did everything with fanatical discipline. Nothing got in the way. No fancy architecture, or ritual, or color to distract from the corporate image of efficiency.
cues.zh: 这些修士以狂热纪律做每件事。没有任何东西挡路。没有花哨的建筑、仪式或色彩来分散对企业效率形象的注意力。

cues.en: And as their lands and their management techniques developed, the news spread to the world outside.
cues.zh: 随着他们的土地和管理技术发展，消息传到了外面的世界。

cues.en: Maybe their single biggest success was their sheep rearing techniques, because by the thirteenth century, they were producing the best wool in Europe.
cues.zh: 也许他们最大的单项成功是养羊技术，因为到13世纪，他们生产出了欧洲最好的羊毛。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 于是

cues.en: there were the Europeans of the twelfth century,
cues.zh: 12世纪的欧洲人便是如此，

cues.en: with all that amazing water power technology and
cues.zh: 拥有那些惊人的水力技术，以及

cues.en: and the red hot industrial management systems worked out by the Cistercians,
cues.zh: 以及西多会修士搞出的火热工业管理体系，

cues.en: almost
cues.zh: 几乎

cues.en: waiting for something to happen,
cues.zh: 在等待某件事发生，

cues.en: something that would
cues.zh: 某件会

cues.en: generate enough money to trigger the economy off into high gear.
cues.zh: 产生足够多的钱，把经济推入高速档。

cues.en: And when that something happened,
cues.zh: 当那件事真正发生时，

cues.en: it was one of those examples of the way change can come about
cues.zh: 它完美诠释了变革是如何

cues.en: quite unexpectedly.
cues.zh: 出人意料地降临的。

cues.en: Because
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: the two inventions that were to trigger the great leap forward
cues.zh: 促成这次大飞跃的两项发明，

cues.en: could never have been foreseen here in Europe,
cues.zh: 在欧洲本土根本无人能够预见，

cues.en: because they came from China.
cues.zh: 因为它们来自中国。

cues.en: The Arabs brought them to us,
cues.zh: 是阿拉伯人把它们带过来的，

cues.en: and what a gift they were.
cues.zh: 这可真是一份厚礼。

cues.en: The first one of those Chinese gifts was a new loom,
cues.zh: 来自中国的首件厚礼是一种新型织机，

cues.en: and it immediately caused a problem.
cues.zh: 它立刻引发了一个新问题。

cues.en: It speeded up weaving because the thread lifting business was now done by foot pedals, not by the weaver's hands anymore.
cues.zh: 它加快了织布速度，因为提线改由脚踏板完成，不再需要织工用手了。

cues.en: The new loom produced cloth so fast,
cues.zh: 这种新织机产布极快，

cues.en: they ran into the problem of not enough yarn.
cues.zh: 以至于他们碰到了纱线不够用的难题。

cues.en: See, up to then, you spun yarn in a way that hadn't changed for centuries. You teased the fibers out of the mass and hand twisted them onto a spindle.
cues.zh: 你看，在那之前，纺纱方式几百年都没变过：先把纤维从团块中理出来，再用手捻到纱锭上。

cues.en: Took hours.
cues.zh: 得花好几个小时。

cues.en: Then, in the thirteenth century, the second Chinese idea arrived and solved the problem, because it produced yarn fast enough to keep up with the new loom.
cues.zh: 接着在13世纪，第二项中国发明传入并解决了难题，它产纱的速度足以跟上新织机。

cues.en: It was the spinning wheel.
cues.zh: 那就是纺车。

cues.en: Early on, they didn't have much more than the wheel and the spindle. Foot pedals came later.
cues.zh: 早期，它基本就只有一个轮子和一个纱锭，脚踏板是后来才加上的。

cues.en: But these two simple bits of machinery fitted together like bits of a jigsaw,
cues.zh: 但这两种简易机械像拼图一样完美契合，

cues.en: and when they did, the places they were used got very, very rich.
cues.zh: 一旦结合，使用它们的地方就变得极其富有。

cues.en: Places like Bruges.
cues.zh: 比如布鲁日（Bruges）。

cues.en: Bruges was one of the richest of the medieval cities built by the woolen trade. And if you know anybody called Draper, boy, were his ancestors well off. The cloth merchants made so much loot, they didn't know what to do with it. They built roads, canals, guild halls, cathedrals.
cues.zh: 布鲁日是靠毛纺织业兴起的中世纪最富庶城市之一。如果你认识姓 Draper 的人，天哪，他的祖先可真是阔绰。布商们赚得盆满钵满，钱多到不知怎么花，于是修路、开运河、建行会大厅和主教座堂。

cues.en: They even had their own laws.
cues.zh: 他们甚至制定了自己的法律。

cues.en: And in spite of all that, they still had enough money left for high technology music.
cues.zh: 即便如此，他们剩的钱还足够投资高科技音乐。

cues.en: Not just this kind of toy, the kind you can still hear in the cathedral towers all over Belgium,
cues.zh: 不只是这种小玩意儿，而是在全比利时的大教堂钟楼里至今仍能听到的那种，

cues.en: where the carillon still plays.
cues.zh: 那里的钟琴（carillon）至今仍在演奏。

cues.en: Recognize the mechanism? It's the cam again, tripping levers that pulled wires that eventually pulled the clapper on one or other of a number of differently tuned bells.
cues.zh: 认出这个机械结构了吗？又是凸轮，它拨动杠杆拉动钢丝，最终拉动一组不同音调钟铃中的钟舌。

cues.en: You set the cams in like pegs to trip certain levers and ring certain bells.
cues.zh: 只要像销钉一样插好凸轮，就能拨动特定杠杆、敲响特定钟铃。

cues.en: Now, the reason all the good burgers had all these extra goodies was because they'd found a new market for their wool.
cues.zh: 这些市民阶层之所以能坐拥这些好东西，是因为他们为自己的羊毛找到了新市场。

cues.en: See, all over Europe, people now had surplus, and surplus always looked for a ready market.
cues.zh: 你瞧，整个欧洲的人们都有了盈余，而盈余总是在寻找现成的销路。

cues.en: South from Scandinavia and England and Flanders came fur and wool and cloth.
cues.zh: 从北边的斯堪的纳维亚、英格兰和法兰德斯向南，运来了皮草、羊毛和布料。

cues.en: North through the Mediterranean, through Genoa and Venice, came silk and spices from the Far East. East from France and Spain came salt, wine, and cordovan leather. And from Russia, fur, I suppose, everybody's crossroads lay in the county of Champagne at four little towns where they set up the first international markets called the Champagne Fairs.
cues.zh: 经地中海穿过热那亚和威尼斯向北，运来了远东的丝绸与香料；从法国和西班牙向东，运来了食盐、葡萄酒和科尔多瓦皮革；还有来自俄罗斯的皮草——我想，所有人的交汇点就在香槟伯国，他们在四个小镇上建起了最早的国际集市，也就是香槟集市（Champagne Fairs）。

cues.en: The biggest fair was held at Troyes, in those days, half the size of London. And merchants turned up because they got a special safe conduct from the king and armed guards along the road.
cues.zh: 当时最大的集市在特鲁瓦举办，规模只有伦敦的一半。商人们会来，是因为他们能从国王那里拿到特别通行证，路上还有武装护卫。

cues.en: Of course, the town made a bit out of it too. You had to pay a license to set up your stall, and there was a sales tax. Isn't the raw ones? And you had to pay to come in and out of town.
cues.zh: 当然，镇子也从中赚了点。摆摊要交执照费，还有销售税。这还不算狠吗？进出城也得交钱。

cues.en: Not that any of this bothered the merchants. They just upped the price.
cues.zh: 这些并没让商人们太在意。他们只是把价格抬高了。

cues.en: Funny how some things don't change.
cues.zh: 有意思的是，有些事就是不会变。

cues.en: Anyway, this international money making went like a house on fire, especially among those able to turn up with the very, very rare stuff, like like silk,
cues.zh: 总之，这种跨国赚钱生意火得不得了，尤其是对那些能带来非常非常稀罕的东西的人，比如丝绸，

cues.en: where you really made a packet.
cues.zh: 那可真能赚一大笔。

cues.en: Most of the really fancy stuff was brought by the Italians who practically ran the place.
cues.zh: 大多数真正高档的东西都是意大利人带来的，他们几乎控制了这里。

cues.en: there were no less than 15 Italian cities who had consulates here in Troyes.
cues.zh: 已有不少于15个意大利城市在特鲁瓦设有领事馆。

cues.en: The reason the Italians mattered so much was because
cues.zh: 意大利人之所以如此重要，是因为

cues.en: when everybody got back from a crusade in the Middle East to their rather dull northern European town,
cues.zh: 当大家从中东十字军东征回来，回到他们相当沉闷的北欧小镇时，

cues.en: All they could talk about were the amazing luxuries of the mysterious Orient, silk,
cues.zh: 他们能聊的全是神秘东方那些令人惊叹的奢侈品，丝绸、

cues.en: cinnamon,
cues.zh: 肉桂、

cues.en: pepper,
cues.zh: 胡椒、

cues.en: elephant tusks,
cues.zh: 象牙、

cues.en: things which the Italians were very well placed to provide at the fairs.
cues.zh: 这些东西，意大利人在集市上正好非常方便供应。

cues.en: The Venetians,
cues.zh: 威尼斯人、

cues.en: the Genoese,
cues.zh: 热那亚人、

cues.en: and the Pisans all had trading colonies all around the Eastern Mediterranean,
cues.zh: 和比萨人，在东地中海周围都有贸易殖民地，

cues.en: where they could pick up stuff from as far away as China.
cues.zh: 他们能从远至中国的地方收来货物。

cues.en: Well, there was so much money to be made here.
cues.zh: 这里能赚的钱太多了。

cues.en: And given the fact that the Genoese have always had a reputation for being where the prophets are, it's not surprising that it was probably they
cues.zh: 考虑到热那亚人一向以“哪儿有利可图，他们就在哪儿”著称，难怪很可能正是他们

cues.en: who came up with a way to keep the financial ball rolling, so to speak, with this thing.
cues.zh: 想出了办法，可以说，用这个东西让金融这盘生意继续转下去。

cues.en: It's an investment contract called a commender.
cues.zh: 这是一种叫康曼达（commenda）的投资合同。

cues.en: Now, this is a copy. But this particular one was written on the 11/14/1244.
cues.zh: 现在，这是一份副本。但这一份写于1244年11月14日。

cues.en: And it's a contract between a traveling merchant called John of the Parish of Saint Ginesius,
cues.zh: 这是一份合同，双方分别是一个叫 John 的行商，来自 Saint Ginesius 教区，

cues.en: and a draper called Otto, there's Otto,
cues.zh: 和一个叫 Otto 的布商，Otto 在这里，

cues.en: who is investing
cues.zh: 他投资

cues.en: Genoese pounds
cues.zh: 热那亚镑

cues.en: as a share in a load of purple cloth and gold silk that John the merchant is bringing up here to the Champagne Fairs.
cues.zh: 作为一份份额，投入一批紫色布料和金色丝绸，由商人 John 运到这里参加香槟集市。

cues.en: The agreement goes on to say that John can use his discretion as to where and when he trades, on condition that when he gets back to Genoa, Otto gets detailed accounts and his share of the profits.
cues.zh: 协议还写明，John 可以自行决定在哪里、何时交易，条件是等他回到热那亚时，Otto 要拿到详细账目和利润分成。

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: tatty bit of paper, which looks like an everyday affair thing you write in the back of an envelope practically,
cues.zh: 一张破破烂烂的纸，几乎就像你随手写在信封背面的日常便条，

cues.en: represents a really fundamental
cues.zh: 却代表着一项真正根本性的

cues.en: innovation.
cues.zh: 创新。

cues.en: Because it brought everybody, rich and poor, who had any spare cash in on the act. And that spread the risk, and that encouraged more merchants to go to more places.
cues.zh: 因为它把任何有闲钱的富人穷人全都拉进了这场生意。这分散了风险，也鼓励更多商人去更多地方。

cues.en: So the champagne fairs and others, places like this, really boomed.
cues.zh: 香槟集市以及其他类似集市，像这样的地方，真的繁荣了起来。

cues.en: It looked as if good times were here to stay.
cues.zh: 看起来好日子会一直持续下去。

cues.en: And then, at the beginning of the fourteenth century,
cues.zh: 可随后，在14世纪初，

cues.en: came a change in the weather,
cues.zh: 天气变了，

cues.en: freezing winters and rainy summers.
cues.zh: 寒冬封冻，夏季多雨。

cues.en: Bad harvests followed, and then famine.
cues.zh: 坏收成接踵而至，随后是饥荒。

cues.en: With little or no surplus crops to sell, money became tight, and the fares began to fail.
cues.zh: 没有或几乎没有余粮可卖，银根紧缩，集市开始衰落。

cues.en: All over Europe, people tightened their belts.
cues.zh: 整个欧洲的人都勒紧了裤腰带。

cues.en: And in this weakened condition,
cues.zh: 在这种虚弱状态下，

cues.en: they were virtually defenseless against attack.
cues.zh: 他们面对侵袭几乎毫无防御能力。

cues.en: And when it came in 1347,
cues.zh: 当它在1347年到来时，

cues.en: the effect was devastating.
cues.zh: 后果是毁灭性的。

cues.en: All the more so, because they had no defense against the enemy.
cues.zh: 更糟的是，他们对这个敌人毫无防御。

cues.en: It was a flea.
cues.zh: 敌人是一只跳蚤。

cues.en: The flea carried the black death. And from when it arrived in Europe in 1347,
cues.zh: 跳蚤携带黑死病。从1347年它抵达欧洲，

cues.en: on board ship from the Crimea,
cues.zh: 由船从克里米亚带来，

cues.en: to when it receded only four years later, it killed maybe forty million people.
cues.zh: 到仅仅四年后它消退，它杀死了大约四千万人。

cues.en: villages were totally wiped out. At the height of the plague, there weren't enough living to bury the dead.
cues.zh: 座村庄被彻底摧毁。瘟疫最严重时，活人都不够埋葬死者。

cues.en: The flea sucked the disease in rat's blood, and when the rat died, it jumped onto people and bit them.
cues.zh: 跳蚤从鼠血中吸进病菌，老鼠一死，它就跳到人身上咬人。

cues.en: The effect was appalling,
cues.zh: 后果骇人听闻，

cues.en: from fever to abscesses in the groin and armpits to death inside twenty four hours. Black pustules spread all over the body, which was why they called it the black death.
cues.zh: 从发烧，到腹股沟和腋下脓肿，再到24小时内死亡。黑色脓疱蔓延全身，所以他们称之为黑死病。

cues.en: The effects were particularly bad in the towns, packed with people busy making all that money. The plague ripped through them.
cues.zh: 城镇里的影响尤其严重，那里挤满了忙着赚大钱的人。瘟疫横扫了他们。

cues.en: And a new face appeared in all the pictures. And for those with itchy feet, a new kind of dance you could unexpectedly find yourself swinging to. The dance of death.
cues.zh: 所有画里都出现了一张新面孔。对坐不住的人来说，还有一种新舞蹈，你会不知不觉跟着摇摆起来。死亡之舞。

cues.en: One grimly enjoyable thing came out of it all. The people who died left their money to the people who lived.
cues.zh: 这一切还带来一件阴森又好玩的后果。死去的人把钱留给了活着的人。

cues.en: All they could hope for was that they'd survive to enjoy it.
cues.zh: 他们只能指望自己能活下来享受这笔钱。

cues.en: Well, no nightmare lasts forever. By 1351,
cues.zh: 噩梦不会永远持续。到1351年，

cues.en: the worst was over.
cues.zh: 最糟的已经过去。

cues.en: When it was all over, the survivors went insane,
cues.zh: 当一切结束时，幸存者都疯了，

cues.en: trying to forget the horror they'd lived through. Life everywhere in Europe became one long hysterical shindig.
cues.zh: 试图忘掉亲历的恐怖。欧洲各地的生活都变成了一场漫长而歇斯底里的狂欢。

cues.en: People spent the money the plague had given them on the wildest outfit they could buy. If you were rich, silk embroidered with gold wire was the thing. The middle classes went into expensive little numbers in wool and velvet. And the peasants,
cues.zh: 人们把瘟疫“给”他们的钱花在能买到的最狂野的装扮上。有钱人穿金线刺绣的丝绸。中产阶级穿起羊毛和天鹅绒的昂贵小件衣服。而农民呢，

cues.en: well, thanks to that loom way back and the fact that flax is cheap to grow, linen was their thing. Well, it was everybody's thing really, in hats and shirts and bed sheets.
cues.zh: 嗯，多亏了早先那台织布机，再加上亚麻种植成本低，亚麻布就是他们的选择。其实它成了所有人的选择——帽子、衬衫、床单都用它。

cues.en: And especially,
cues.zh: 尤其是，

cues.en: if you take an indiscreet look up the nearest girl's skirt,
cues.zh: 如果你冒失地往最近一个女孩的裙底看一眼，

cues.en: that,
cues.zh: 那个，

cues.en: underwear.
cues.zh: 内衣。

cues.en: And just this once, that's the great trigger of change, what you're looking at now. Yes,
cues.zh: 而就这一次，那就是变革的巨大触发点，也就是你现在看到的东西。没错，

cues.en: frilly knickers.
cues.zh: 花边内裤。

cues.en: This is the first result of the great fourteenth century bed linen and underwear boom.
cues.zh: 这就是14世纪床单和内衣大繁荣的第一个成果。

cues.en: The guy who used to go around collecting bones for fertilizer now started collecting linen too. He became a rag and bone man. Why?
cues.zh: 以前到处收骨头做肥料的人，现在也开始收亚麻破布了。他成了收破烂的。为什么呢？

cues.en: Well, that's the second result of everybody wearing woolen, because when they wore it out, they threw it away. So there was this great pile of linen rag.
cues.zh: 这是人人都穿毛衣的第二个结果，因为衣服穿破后大家就会扔掉。于是就有了大堆大堆的亚麻破布。

cues.en: And guess who went bananas about that?
cues.zh: 猜猜谁对此乐疯了？

cues.en: Okay. Let me give you a clue. The first thing that happens to the linen in this process is that they take it and rip it against a knife to make the rags even smaller.
cues.zh: 好吧，给你们点提示。在这个工序中，处理亚麻的第一步，就是拿刀把它割得更碎。

cues.en: And what is shredded linen rag absolutely perfect for making?
cues.zh: 那么，撕碎的亚麻破布最适合拿来做什么？

cues.en: Yes, paper.
cues.zh: 没错，造纸。

cues.en: So the papermakers got an unexpected linen rag bonanza,
cues.zh: 于是造纸工匠意外迎来了一场破布狂欢，

cues.en: pounded by hammers, tripped again
cues.zh: 被大锤反复敲打，

cues.en: by the can.
cues.zh: 由凸轮不断带动。

cues.en: You bash the rag in water and gum for forty eight hours, and the sludge you get is paper pulp.
cues.zh: 把破布浸在水和树胶里捶打48小时，得到的浆状物就是纸浆。

cues.en: Slosh that onto a wire mesh frame,
cues.zh: 把纸浆泼在铁丝网筛框上，

cues.en: count five, and you've got yourself a sheet of paper. Well, a sheet of very wet paper.
cues.zh: 数到五，你就得到了一张纸。好吧，一张湿漉漉的纸。

cues.en: So the next thing you do, no prices, is dry it.
cues.zh: 接下来要做的事，毫无悬念，就是晾干。

cues.en: Funny coincidence, the wire mesh frame. A lot of wire makers about making all that gold embroidery people had started wearing.
cues.zh: 铁丝网筛框是个有趣的巧合。当时周围有很多拉丝工，在为人们流行佩戴的金线刺绣制作金属丝。

cues.en: Anyway, the paper. You lay each sheet between layers of wool and cloth to soak up the moisture.
cues.zh: 言归正传，说回纸。你把每张纸夹在羊毛和布料之间来吸干水分。

cues.en: Looks more like a sheet of porridge, doesn't it?
cues.zh: 看着倒更像一摊烂粥，对吧？

cues.en: And when you've got a big pile of wool and wet paper sandwiches stacked up, you call the lads.
cues.zh: 等把羊毛和湿纸一层层叠成厚厚一摞，你就把伙计们叫过来。

cues.en: All you do now is squeeze the pile in a press until you've got nearly all the water out of the paper when you hang it up to dry, and that's all there is to it.
cues.zh: 现在只需用压榨机把这堆东西压实，挤出纸里几乎所有的水分，然后挂起来晾干，大功告成。

cues.en: Funny how it all comes together here in the paper mill. The water power to run the cams tripping the hammers to make the pulp, the wine press come linen press to squeeze out the water, and thanks to the automatic loom, the linen that makes the pulp. And because of all that free linen, suddenly, the cheapest thing around
cues.zh: 巧妙的是，这一切都在造纸作坊里交汇了。用水力驱动凸轮带动水锤捣成纸浆，用榨酒机改造成的压布机挤出水分，加上全靠自动织布机才有的亚麻纸浆。正因为这些免费的亚麻，突然之间，市面上最便宜的东西

cues.en: was paper.
cues.zh: 变成了纸。

cues.en: This is one of those moments in history when things come together like a jigsaw to produce something
cues.zh: 这是历史上的奇妙时刻之一，各种零散的事物像拼图一样拼合在一起，催生出了

cues.en: something entirely new.
cues.zh: 一种全新的东西。

cues.en: Look at the bits we've got so far. Because of the linen, we have cheap paper.
cues.zh: 看看我们目前拼出的部分：有了亚麻，我们有了便宜的纸。

cues.en: The Black Death is just over, so the
cues.zh: 黑死病刚刚过去，

cues.en: economy of Europe is on the up and up. Administration is expanding.
cues.zh: 欧洲的经济正在蒸蒸日上。行政管理体系不断扩张。

cues.en: There are many more clerks needed to do all the paperwork. However,
cues.zh: 需要大量文员来处理文书工作。然而，

cues.en: the Black Death has killed half the clerks off,
cues.zh: 黑死病夺走了一半文员的性命，

cues.en: so they cost a great deal.
cues.zh: 导致雇佣他们的成本极其高昂。

cues.en: So we have extremely cheap paper, and the cost of a man who writes on it has gone up astronomically.
cues.zh: 于是，我们有了极其便宜的纸，但在纸上抄写的人工成本却暴涨到了天价。

cues.en: What do you need to solve that problem?
cues.zh: 要解决这个问题，你需要什么？

cues.en: Yes. Printing.
cues.zh: 没错。印刷术。

cues.en: And that's exactly what happened.
cues.zh: 事实正是如此。

cues.en: But before the final bit of the jigsaw could be put into place, you needed one particular skill, the kind of skill, say, a goldsmith has.
cues.zh: 但在拼上最后这块拼图之前，你还需要一种特殊的技能，比方说，金匠才掌握的那种手艺。

cues.en: If you come upstairs with me, I'll show you what I mean.
cues.zh: 如果你跟我上楼，我就让你看看我的意思。

cues.en: You see,
cues.zh: 你看，

cues.en: printing had been around for centuries, in the case of the Chinese, for a thousand years, but it was printing with blocks like this.
cues.zh: 印刷术已经存在了几个世纪，对中国来说，已经有一千年了，但那是用这样的木块来印刷。

cues.en: The trouble was those blocks being made of of wood would tend to wear down, and in any case, they only did the one thing.
cues.zh: 问题在于，那些木块是用木头做的，容易磨损，而且不管怎样，它们只能做一件事。

cues.en: Now what our
cues.zh: 那么，我们的

cues.en: goldsmith friend did, and by the way, his name was Johann Gutenberg, and he lived in Mainz in Germany in fourteen fifties,
cues.zh: 金匠朋友做了什么呢，顺便说一句，他叫 Johann Gutenberg，住在 1450 年代德国美因茨，

cues.en: He used his expertise with precious metal. He knew what that was, the hallmark.
cues.zh: 他运用了自己在贵金属方面的专长。他知道那是什么，就是金银纯度印记。

cues.en: And he knew that the hallmark was made with a punch. So he took a punch,
cues.zh: 他知道金银纯度印记是用冲头打出来的。于是他拿了一个冲头，

cues.en: and he carved a letter on the end of it, and using the punch, he punched that letter into a soft copper bar.
cues.zh: 在冲头末端刻上一个字母，然后用冲头把这个字母冲进一根软铜条。

cues.en: Then he designed
cues.zh: 然后他设计

cues.en: a mold in two bits so that it comes apart. You put the mold together like that,
cues.zh: 一个可拆开的两半模具。你把模具这样合起来，

cues.en: you slide into the mold the letter you want to make, any letter,
cues.zh: 把你想做的字母，任何字母，插进模具里，

cues.en: close it tight with a big spring,
cues.zh: 用一个大弹簧把它压紧，

cues.en: turn it over,
cues.zh: 把它翻转过来，

cues.en: and then very, very carefully,
cues.zh: 然后非常非常小心地，

cues.en: you put
cues.zh: 你把

cues.en: molten
cues.zh: 熔化的

cues.en: lead alloy
cues.zh: 铅合金

cues.en: into the mold like this.
cues.zh: 像这样倒进模具里。

cues.en: Leave it for just a few seconds,
cues.zh: 等几秒钟，

cues.en: and then you break the mold,
cues.zh: 然后你打开模具，

cues.en: and the letter
cues.zh: 那个字母

cues.en: is there,
cues.zh: 就在那里，

cues.en: ready
cues.zh: 准备好

cues.en: to
cues.zh: 用来

cues.en: print with.
cues.zh: 印刷了。

cues.en: And that letter a will go anywhere on the page you want to put a letter a. It will go in the place of any other letter a. The mold makes all the letters so they're all the same size. It makes all the spaces so they're all the same size. So the printing is uniform.
cues.zh: 那个字母 a 可以放到页面上任何你想放字母 a 的位置。它可以替换任何其他字母 a。模具造出的所有字母大小都一样。它造出的所有空格也大小都一样。所以印刷是统一的。

cues.en: But it's the interchangeability of the letters that is at the heart of Gutenberg's invention.
cues.zh: 但正是字母的可互换性，才是 Gutenberg 发明的核心。

cues.en: If you think about it, it was a good deal easier for a European to do than, say, for a Chinese.
cues.zh: 你想想看，这对欧洲人来说，要比比如说对中国人容易得多。

cues.en: Because the Chinese language has thousands of characters. And if you made every one of them, you need a space
cues.zh: 因为汉语有成千上万个字。如果要制作每一个字，你需要一块

cues.en: as big as this printing room in Antwerp just to store them in. Whereas the the Latin alphabet at the time only had 23 letters to be made.
cues.zh: 像安特卫普这间印刷室一样大的地方，才装得下它们。而当时的拉丁字母只需要制作 23 个字母。

cues.en: As for the printing itself, well, that was a bit of a cinch. This press
cues.zh: 至于印刷本身，嗯，那还算轻而易举。这台压印机

cues.en: was just an adaptation
cues.zh: 只是改造自

cues.en: of a linen press
cues.zh: 一台亚麻布压机

cues.en: that had been around for centuries,
cues.zh: 它已经存在了几百年，

cues.en: as had the
cues.zh: 同样如此的还有

cues.en: ink
cues.zh: 墨水

cues.en: and the paper.
cues.zh: 和纸张。

cues.en: This
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 是

cues.en: the first
cues.zh: 第一件

cues.en: dated piece of printing we know of.
cues.zh: 我们所知有明确日期的印刷品。

cues.en: It's... There may be earlier ones, but this one has a date on it.
cues.zh: 它……可能还有更早的，但这一件上面有日期。

cues.en: And the people who did it were very proud of what they've done. It's the introduction
cues.zh: 做这件事的人非常为自己所做的感到自豪。这是……的引言

cues.en: to a book of Psalms.
cues.zh: 一本《诗篇》书。

cues.en: And the text says,
cues.zh: 文字写道，

cues.en: this work,
cues.zh: 这部作品，

cues.en: adorned with the magnificence of capital letters,
cues.zh: 以大写字母的华美装饰，

cues.en: was fashioned with the use of a mechanical process for printing and making letters without the use of a pen.
cues.zh: 是用机械工艺印刷和制作字母而成，无需使用笔。

cues.en: And then it says, name the of the two many were so proud of what they'd done. Joachim
cues.zh: 然后它写道，点出这两位非常为自己所做之事感到自豪的人的名字。Joachim

cues.en: Furst
cues.zh: Furst

cues.en: and Peter Schefer.
cues.zh: 和 Peter Schefer。

cues.en: And then the date, 08/14/1457.
The coming of the book changed everything.
cues.zh: 书籍的出现改变了一切。

cues.en: Perhaps the most obvious change was the appearance of the bookshop where you could come in and buy anything you wanted to read.
cues.zh: 也许最明显的变化，是书店出现了：你可以走进去，买任何想读的东西。

cues.en: Knowledge was no longer the private property of of the priest or the prince or the scholar.
cues.zh: 知识不再只是教士、王公或学者的私有财产。

cues.en: If you could pay and you could read,
cues.zh: 只要付得起钱、识得了字，

cues.en: it was all yours.
cues.zh: 一切就都归你。

cues.en: The new books also standardized
cues.zh: 新书还统一了

cues.en: spelling.
cues.zh: 拼写。

cues.en: They carried an author's name,
cues.zh: 书上印着作者的名字，

cues.en: and they encouraged accuracy because the books could be widely read by people who knew more about the subject perhaps than the author himself.
cues.zh: 也促使内容更准确，因为这些书可能被广泛阅读，而读者对相关主题的了解也许比作者本人还多。

cues.en: But perhaps most fundamental of all, the new books gave birth to the specialization
cues.zh: 但或许最根本的是，新书催生了专业化，

cues.en: that is the the blessing or or the bane, depending on your point of view, of our modern world.
cues.zh: 这正是现代世界的福分，或者祸根，取决于你怎么看。

cues.en: Because, you see, the architects and the engineers started to write about what they knew in terms that only their co professionals would understand.
cues.zh: 因为，你看，建筑师和工程师开始用只有同行才懂的语言，写下他们所知的东西。

cues.en: The generation that that first read these new books
cues.zh: 第一批读到这些新书的那一代人，

cues.en: could as easily turn its hand to the lute
cues.zh: 同样能轻松地弹起鲁特琴，

cues.en: or the sword or the architect's drawing.
cues.zh: 或挥剑，或画建筑图。

cues.en: And because of printing, they were the last generation to be able to do that.
cues.zh: 而因为印刷术，他们成了最后一代能做到这一点的人。

cues.en: The coming of the books must have seemed as if it was going to turn the world upside down
cues.zh: 书籍的到来，当时看起来仿佛会颠覆世界——

cues.en: in the way it spread and and democratized
cues.zh: 以它传播并民主化

cues.en: knowledge.
cues.zh: 知识的方式。

cues.en: And one of the few men responsible for that spread was an Italian called Aldus Minutius. Now he realized that what people needed and wanted
cues.zh: 推动这种传播的少数人之一，是一个叫 Aldus Minutius 的意大利人。他意识到，人们需要也想要的是

cues.en: was cheap,
cues.zh: 便宜的、

cues.en: standard books that they could carry with them anywhere they went in their saddlebags. And so he produced the world's first pocket edition.
cues.zh: 能放进马鞍袋、随身带到任何地方的标准书。于是他做出了世界上第一本袖珍版。

cues.en: And he did so in what, by 1500, was the printing capital of Europe,
cues.zh: 他是在 1500 年时的欧洲印刷之都做成的，

cues.en: Venice.
cues.zh: 威尼斯。

cues.en: Used to blow their own trumpet a lot, the sixteenth century Venetians.
cues.zh: 十六世纪的威尼斯人很爱自吹自擂。

cues.en: Well, you couldn't blame them. There were, after all, more millionaires
cues.zh: 嗯，这也不能怪他们。毕竟这里有更多百万富翁，

cues.en: per square inch here than anywhere else in Europe.
cues.zh: 按每平方英寸算，比欧洲任何地方都多。

cues.en: Biggest navy, biggest overseas commercial empire, biggest bank balance,
cues.zh: 最大的海军、最大的海外商业帝国、最多的银行存款，

cues.en: Venice was queen of the seas.
cues.zh: 威尼斯是海洋女王。

cues.en: Of course, there was nowhere else she could have been queen of. Not much land in Venice.
cues.zh: 当然，她也没别的地方能当女王。威尼斯没多少陆地。

cues.en: She was a city full of businessmen,
cues.zh: 这是一座满是商人的城市，

cues.en: and because of her connections with Constantinople,
cues.zh: 又因为她与君士坦丁堡的联系，

cues.en: she was also full of Greeks, refugees
cues.zh: 城里也满是希腊人，都是难民，

cues.en: from when the Turks invaded it in 1453.
cues.zh: 是在 1453 年土耳其人入侵时逃来的。

cues.en: And it was the Greek connection that gave the printer Aldus Minutius his big chance.
cues.zh: 正是与希腊人的联系，给了印刷商 Aldus Minutius 大好机会。

cues.en: Because Aldis got the Greek refugees to work for him, and because of that, his books gave the world a taste for the knowledge and the style of ancient Greece.
cues.zh: 因为 Aldis 让希腊难民为他工作，也正因如此，他的书让世界领略到古希腊的知识与风格。

cues.en: He turned out dictionaries and grammar books first, so his customers could learn Greek, and then, of course, they could move on to reading the Greek books he would sell them. No fool he.
cues.zh: 他先推出词典和语法书，让顾客学会希腊语；然后，他们当然就能接着读他卖给他们的希腊文书。他可不傻。

cues.en: Well, the new books got everybody turned on to matters ancient. One of the earliest bestsellers was a Roman thing on architecture
cues.zh: 新书让大家对古代事物产生了浓厚兴趣。最早的畅销书之一是关于建筑的古罗马著作，

cues.en: that got people into big prestige building projects, people like Michelangelo.
cues.zh: 它带动人们投身于大型面子建筑工程，比如 Michelangelo 这样的人。

cues.en: Thanks to Aldus and the Venetian printing presses, in 1500,
cues.zh: 得益于 Aldus 和威尼斯的印刷工坊，到了1500年，

cues.en: only fifty years after Gutenberg,
cues.zh: 距离 Gutenberg 仅五十年后，

cues.en: there were no less than 20,000,000 books in existence.
cues.zh: 世上存在的书籍就已经不下两千万本了。

cues.en: Aldus died.
cues.zh: Aldus 去世了。

cues.en: Aldus Magnetius was laid to rest with his books heaped around him as a mark of respect for what he'd done, which was to print every major Greek classic in existence and invent a new kind of letter type for his pocket editions. It was a kind of print that would pack a lot into a tight space. We call it italic.
cues.zh: Aldus Magnetius 安息时身旁堆满了他的书，以致敬他的贡献——他印制了现存所有的古希腊主要经典，还为他的袖珍版图书发明了一种新字体。这种字体能在狭小空间里排下很多字，我们称之为斜体。

cues.en: So now the world could start worrying about something it had never had to worry about before,
cues.zh: 于是，世人可以开始操心以前从未操心过的事情了——

cues.en: the small print.
cues.zh: 密密麻麻的小字印刷。

cues.en: But above all, thanks to books, the world learnt about Greek science.
cues.zh: 但最重要的是，多亏了书籍，世界得以了解希腊科学。

cues.en: This was one of the books that made the greatest impact of all by the Greek hero of Alexandria.
cues.zh: 其中影响最深远的书籍之一，出自古希腊的 Hero of Alexandria。

cues.en: It details how to make machines using the natural forces of air or steam or water as power sources. It's really talking about complicated toys.
cues.zh: 它详细介绍了如何利用空气、蒸汽或水等自然力作为动力源来制造机器。其实讲的就是些复杂的玩具。

cues.en: But this book and others like it put the world of Greek science and the ancient past into the hands of the armorers and the architects and the engineers working for the princes and bishops of sixteenth century Italy.
cues.zh: 但这本书以及同类书籍，把古希腊科学与远古世界送到了16世纪意大利为君主和主教效力的盔甲匠、建筑师和工程师手中。

cues.en: And look how the armor is immediately beginning to work in the antique style. On this tapestry, this bunch of soldiers, they're using the latest in handguns,
cues.zh: 瞧这盔甲，立刻开始走复古风格了。在这幅挂毯上，这群士兵用着最新式的轻武器，

cues.en: and yet they themselves
cues.zh: 可他们自己

cues.en: are dressed like Caesar's centurions.
cues.zh: 穿戴得却像 Caesar 的百夫长。

cues.en: As the the wealth of the mysterious East and West began to pour into Europe, and the population began to soar, the princes also began to embellish their growing cities with elaborate water supply systems,
cues.zh: 随着神秘东西方的财富源源不断涌入欧洲，人口开始激增，君主们也开始用精密的供水系统来装点不断扩张的城市，

cues.en: operated by the same mechanical devices
cues.zh: 这些系统运作所用的机械装置，

cues.en: as were shown in the Greek and Roman books. And in their homes, the aristocrats would hang tapestries like this one, containing scenes of fantastic inventions like the flying throne being carried into the sky by winged beasts that can never quite make the piece of ham above their heads.
cues.zh: 正与希腊和罗马典籍里展示的一模一样。在宅邸中，贵族们会挂上类似这样的挂毯，上面描绘着奇幻发明的场景——比如飞天宝座被带翅膀的怪兽拉上天空，怪兽却永远够不到头顶上的那块火腿。

cues.en: Or the mythical story of Alexander the Great exploring the oceans
cues.zh: 抑或是关于 Alexander the Great 探索大洋的、

cues.en: on board a submarine.
cues.zh: 乘坐潜艇的神话故事。

cues.en: What the princes wanted were things, toys, that would show off their their wealth and position in a way that would amuse and impress their friends.
cues.zh: 君主们想要的，是既能炫耀财富和地位、又能逗乐并震慑朋友的玩意儿和玩具。

cues.en: And now, their armorers and their engineers had the techniques to do it.
cues.zh: 而现在，他们的盔甲匠和工程师拥有了实现这一目标的技术。

cues.en: One of the most famous armorers of the time, a fellow called Bartholomew
cues.zh: 当时最著名的盔甲匠之一，一个叫 Bartholomew

cues.en: Campi,
cues.zh: Campi 的人，

cues.en: switched, for example, from making this rather complex armor, the gauntlet,
cues.zh: 就比如从制作这种相当复杂的盔甲手套，

cues.en: to making things like this.
cues.zh: 转向了制作类似这样的东西。

cues.en: It's a clockwork tortoise carrying the god Poseidon,
cues.zh: 这是一只背着海神 Poseidon 的发条乌龟，

cues.en: and it was used at the dinner table
cues.zh: 当时是用在餐桌上的，

cues.en: because they would set it down,
cues.zh: 人们把它放在桌上，

cues.en: and it would take toothpicks from one guest to another around the table.
cues.zh: 它就会绕着桌子，把牙签从一个客人送到另一个客人手里。

cues.en: The vogue for automatic machines spread everywhere,
cues.zh: 对自动机械的狂热风靡各地，

cues.en: and with the help of the hydraulic engineers, it spread in a form that would bring people hundreds of miles just to take a look.
cues.zh: 在水利工程师的助力下，这种风潮演变成能吸引人们从数百英里外赶来一睹为快的奇观。

cues.en: This is one of the best ones still working, the Castle Of Helbrunn outside Salzburg,
cues.zh: 这是现存运转最好的杰作之一，位于 Salzburg 郊外的 Castle Of Helbrunn，

cues.en: built in 1615 so the prince archbishop and his guests could have a little water powered fun and games.
cues.zh: 建于1615年，是为大主教大公和他的宾客提供水力娱乐消遣而建的。

cues.en: The whole place works on water turbines running the familiar cylinder with pegs in it, operating sixteenth century Disneyland.
cues.zh: 整个地方全靠水轮机驱动那种带有凸点的圆柱桶，运转着一座16世纪的“迪士尼乐园”。

cues.en: The name of the game was to get the most unexpected things to spurt water all over the suckers who come to dinner. Everybody laugh because the host was a prince.
cues.zh: 它的精髓就在于：从最意想不到的地方喷水，把来赴宴的倒霉蛋浇个透。大家还得赔笑，因为主人可是大公。

cues.en: And besides,
cues.zh: 再说了，

cues.en: you got a free meal out of it all. Well, that's not all you got out of it.
cues.zh: 毕竟还能蹭顿霸王餐。好吧，你得到的还不止这些。

cues.en: Of course, you couldn't get up until the prince did, and of course, he
cues.zh: 当然，大公不起身，你就不能离席；而他当然

cues.en: didn't need to.
cues.zh: 根本用不着站起来。

cues.en: The craze for automatic machinery that spread through Europe came here too, of course. Here, the pegged cylinders run an entire village of mechanical puppets,
cues.zh: 席卷欧洲的自动机械狂热当然也传到了这里。在这里，带凸点的滚筒驱动着一整个村庄的机械木偶，

cues.en: working like the carillon in Belgium did on wires and levers.
cues.zh: 像比利时的钟琴一样，通过拉线和杠杆运转。

cues.en: The whole thing's only 18 feet wide, and they packed a 113 little people into that space.
cues.zh: 整个装置只有18英尺宽，他们却在这个空间里塞进了113个小人偶。

cues.en: Over the top of all this water powered wizardry, there was a mechanical organ to drown the machinery noise,
cues.zh: 在这套神奇的水力机械之上，还有一台机械管风琴来掩盖机器的噪音，

cues.en: and as you left, the prince would politely raise his hat.
cues.zh: 等你离开时，机械大公还会礼貌地脱帽致意。

cues.en: Mechanical organs and things might have stayed just that if it hadn't been for another craze sweeping Europe, a mania for Chinese fashions, particularly in dress,
cues.zh: 要不是另一股席卷欧洲的狂热——对中国风尚，尤其是服饰的痴迷——机械管风琴这类东西可能也就仅止于此了，

cues.en: when at the beginning of the eighteenth century,
cues.zh: 当时正值18世纪初，

cues.en: complicated patterns became all the rage, especially in France, and particularly in silk.
cues.zh: 复杂的图案风靡一时，尤其是在法国，特别是丝绸制品。

cues.en: By the beginning of the eighteenth century, the demand for this kind of pattern was giving the silk weavers of Lyon a real headache. Because silk weaving isn't just a simple over and under business of ordinary weaving, it's much more complicated. I mean, take a look at this. This already complicated pattern, if you follow it across,
cues.zh: 到18世纪初，对这种图案的需求让 Lyon 的丝织工人大伤脑筋。因为丝织可不是普通织布那样简单的一上一下穿梭，它要复杂得多。瞧瞧这个，这么复杂的图案，顺着横向看过去，

cues.en: there, you see suddenly for about five threads, that particular orange.
cues.zh: 看，突然有大概五根经线出现了一截特殊的橙色。

cues.en: So it comes in, say, at thread
cues.zh: 比如它在第
530 根线切入，

cues.en: and it disappears again at thread 535.
cues.zh: 又在第 535 根线消失。

cues.en: Now, if you get that one thread wrong, you've blown it.
cues.zh: 哪怕弄错一根线，整块布就全毁了。

cues.en: Let me show you on this little model loom here how they cracked that problem.
cues.zh: 让我用这台织布机小模型给你们展示一下他们是怎么解决这个难题的。

cues.en: Every thread runs through a tiny ring on a cord. So that if you want to lift the thread, you pull the cord up, the thread lifts, and in this case, the crossing thread would go underneath, and in the final pattern not be seen. Now, if you tie together all the cords for all the threads that you want to lift into one bunch, then one pull will lift them all like this.
cues.zh: 每根线都穿过细绳上的一个小环。只要拉起细绳，这根线就会被提起来，这样穿过去的横线就会走到下方，在最终的图案上隐去。现在，如果你把所有需要提起的线对应的细绳绑成一束，那么只要一拉，就能像这样把它们全部提起。

cues.en: Now, in a complicated pattern, there would be a lot of those cords to pull, and the children whose job it was to do it would get tired and pull their own cords and maybe ruin a week's work. So in 1725,
cues.zh: 要是织造复杂的图案，就得拉动很多绳子，负责拉绳的童工一累，难免拉错绳子，毁掉整整一周的活儿。于是在 1725 年，

cues.en: a Leonese weaver called Basile Bouchon solved the problem because his father was an organ builder.
cues.zh: 里昂一位名叫 Basile Bouchon 的织工解决了这个问题，因为他的父亲是一位管风琴制造匠。

cues.en: Because his father used these things for his automated organs.
cues.zh: 他的父亲在制造自动管风琴时就用过这种装置。

cues.en: Remember the organs? Use the same cylinder with pegs in it to make music as they'd used in Belgium to work their bell ringing carry on. And they'd originally got that idea from the cams set onto the shaft of the paper mill.
cues.zh: 还记得那些管风琴吗？用带栓钉的滚筒来奏乐，跟比利时用来控制钟乐演奏的装置一模一样。而这个创意的源头，其实是造纸厂轮轴上的凸轮。

cues.en: Bouchon saw that the piece of paper that you give to the carpenter to tell him where to put these pegs on the cylinder was in fact
cues.zh: Bouchon 发现，给木匠用来标明滚筒上插栓位置的那张纸，实际上

cues.en: a kind of control mechanism.
cues.zh: 就是一种控制机制。

cues.en: So he put it on a loop.
cues.zh: 于是他把它做成了闭合的环形纸带。

cues.en: Look.
cues.zh: 看。

cues.en: Each control cord comes over and down here.
cues.zh: 每根控制绳都从上方绕过来，落到这里。

cues.en: And whether or not it's moved depends on this horizontal needle here.
cues.zh: 而它是否移动，完全取决于这里的水平横针。

cues.en: Okay, now for the control mechanism part.
cues.zh: 好了，现在来看控制机制部分。

cues.en: What Basile Bouchon did was put a roll of perforated paper
cues.zh: Basile Bouchon 所做的，就是把一卷打孔纸

cues.en: up against the needles, the cross needles.
cues.zh: 顶在这些横针上。

cues.en: And where there was a hole, the needles stayed put because they came through the holes. And where there was not a hole, as in the case of these four needles here,
cues.zh: 有孔的地方，横针穿过小孔保持不动；没孔的地方，就像这四根针一样，

cues.en: the paper pushed the cross needles so that all four needles and all their threads operated simultaneously
cues.zh: 纸会顶住横针，让这四根针以及它们连带的所有经线同时联动，

cues.en: like this.
cues.zh: 就像这样。

cues.en: And to change the pattern, you simply moved the paper along one row of holes. But the paper tore and the weavers placed it in the wrong position. So around 1740,
cues.zh: 要切换花型，只需将纸移动一排孔。但纸容易破损，织工也经常放错位置。于是在 1740 年前后，

cues.en: another weaver from Lyon called Falcon came
cues.zh: 另一位名叫 Falcon 的里昂织工提出了

cues.en: up with this idea. He put each pattern on a separate card. Now the card was more durable,
cues.zh: 这样一个点子。他把每个花样做成单独的卡片。卡片耐用得多，

cues.en: and you couldn't really mistake how you should position it.
cues.zh: 而且基本不可能放错位置。

cues.en: Around 1750,
cues.zh: 到了 1750 年左右，

cues.en: one of the greatest machine makers of all time, a man called Vaux Canson, who was also the inspector for silk factories, automated the entire process.
cues.zh: 史上最伟大的机械发明家之一、时任丝绸工厂督察员的 Vaux Canson，将整个流程实现了全自动化。

cues.en: He put the perforated roll around a cylinder, mounted the cylinder on a chassis, which went backwards and forwards on water power like this. And as it did so, it clicked forward one row of holes automatically
cues.zh: 他把打孔纸卷包在滚筒上，将滚筒安装在底架上，依靠水力像这样前后往复运动。每运动一次，它就会自动咔哒前移一排孔，

cues.en: each time.
cues.zh: 每次都是如此。

cues.en: Now, that was limited to how much paper you could put around the cylinder, and it put men out of work. So for nearly fifty years,
cues.zh: 不过，这受限于滚筒上能卷多少纸，而且还让工人们丢了饭碗。所以在近五十年的时间里，

cues.en: this loom moldered unnoticed here in the Paris Museum of Arts and Crafts. Until just after 1800,
cues.zh: 这台织机默默无闻地在巴黎工艺博物馆里落灰。直到 1800 年刚过，

cues.en: another weaver who happened to be here at the time was asked to put it together. And in doing so, he made a few changes.
cues.zh: 当时恰好在这里的另一位织工被请来组装它。在组装过程中，他做了一些改进。

cues.en: He put Vaux Consohn's idea together with Falcons cards and came up with this.
cues.zh: 他把 Vaux Consohn 的构想与 Falcon 的卡片结合起来，做出了这个。

cues.en: It's automated,
cues.zh: 它是全自动的，

cues.en: and it has the advantage that if you want to increase the pattern, you simply add more cards.
cues.zh: 而且最大的优势在于，如果想扩充图案，只需添加更多卡片即可。

cues.en: Now, for that minor amendment, he got all the glory. Because to this day, the entire
cues.zh: 就因为那点小小的改进，他享尽了所有的荣耀。因为直到今天，整个

cues.en: concept is named after this man. This is a Jacquard Loom.
cues.zh: 概念都是以他命名的。这就是 Jacquard 织布机。

cues.en: And boy, what a success that was.
cues.zh: 天哪，它当年取得了多么巨大的成功。

cues.en: Well, not in France, because the revolutionaries decided they didn't like fancy aristocratic patterns,
cues.zh: 好吧，在法国倒不是，因为革命者们排斥那些花哨的贵族花纹，

cues.en: but in England, where the loom ended up making things like paisley shawls, very popular,
cues.zh: 但在英国大受欢迎，织机最终被用来生产极为畅销的佩斯利披肩，

cues.en: and where these cards got picked up for a very different reason. They got used to control automatic riveting machines
cues.zh: 而且在英国，这些卡片因为一个截然不同的原因被重新起用。它们被用来控制自动铆接机，

cues.en: that by the mid nineteenth century helped to build the great new iron ships that were to make the crossing of the Atlantic safer and faster.
cues.zh: 到了19世纪中叶，这些机器协助造出了崭新的大型铁甲舰，使横渡大西洋变得更安全、更快捷。

cues.en: Just in time to handle the biggest load of passengers that any shipping lines have ever carried.
cues.zh: 正好赶上运送所有航运史上规模最大的客流。

cues.en: The poor, huddled masses of Europe.
cues.zh: 欧洲那些贫困、拥挤的底层大众。

cues.en: And though they didn't know it, these immigrants were to trigger off the development of one of the modern world's most extraordinary invention.
cues.zh: 虽然他们并不知道，但正是这批移民，将促成现代世界最非凡的发明之一。

cues.en: By the eighteen seventies, the immigrants were stepping ashore on American soil at a rate of over 7,000
cues.zh: 到了19世纪70年代，踏上美国土地的移民每天多达 7,000

cues.en: every day.
cues.zh: 人。

cues.en: The journey across the Atlantic had taken anything from twelve days to three weeks, and most of them traveled in conditions that varied from bad to appalling.
cues.zh: 横渡大西洋的航程要花上12天到三周不等，他们大多数人的出行环境从糟糕到骇人听闻。

cues.en: Many of the bigger ships were designed with only one thing in mind, to carry as many immigrants as possible.
cues.zh: 许多大船在设计时只考虑一件事：尽可能多塞进移民。

cues.en: And so
cues.zh: 于是，

cues.en: they came,
cues.zh: 他们来了，

cues.en: in filth and degradation,
cues.zh: 在污秽与屈辱之中，

cues.en: packed in like cattle, treated much the same.
cues.zh: 像牲口一样挤作一团，待遇也相差无几。

cues.en: The vast majority came to New York,
cues.zh: 绝大多数人来到了纽约，

cues.en: at first to the immigration depot at Castle Garden,
cues.zh: 起初是去 Castle Garden 的移民检查站，

cues.en: and then later,
cues.zh: 后来，

cues.en: here, to the place that was to become a symbol both of everything that America offered
cues.zh: 则是来到了这里，这个地方后来成了一个象征，既象征着美国能给予的一切，

cues.en: and the terrible fear
cues.zh: 也象征着那种可怕的恐惧——

cues.en: that at the very gates of freedom,
cues.zh: 害怕就在这自由的大门前，

cues.en: they would be turned away.
cues.zh: 自己会被拒之门外。

cues.en: Here
cues.zh: 就在这里，

cues.en: at Ellis Island.
cues.zh: 在 Ellis Island。

cues.en: It took only a few hours to be accepted or rejected.
cues.zh: 被接纳还是被拒绝，只需要短短几个小时。

cues.en: And much of that time is spent
cues.zh: 而其中大部分时间都耗在

cues.en: and bewildered waiting,
cues.zh: 茫然不知所措的等待中，

cues.en: clutching their cardboard suitcases
cues.zh: 紧攥着自己的纸板行李箱，

cues.en: tied up with string.
cues.zh: 上面用细绳捆着。

cues.en: Everything they possessed.
cues.zh: 那就是他们所有的家当。

cues.en: Some of them, those who could write,
cues.zh: 他们当中的一些人，那些识字的，

cues.en: even left their names on the walls.
cues.zh: 甚至在墙上留下了自己的名字。

cues.en: As if to say,
cues.zh: 仿佛在说，

cues.en: look,
cues.zh: 看啊，

cues.en: I'm ready.
cues.zh: 我准备好了。

cues.en: And then came the moment of truth. The point at which they either passed or failed
cues.zh: 接着就到了见分晓的时刻。那是他们决定成败的关口——

cues.en: the test to become American.
cues.zh: 通往成为美国人的考验。

cues.en: What none of them could have known was how easy that test was.
cues.zh: 可他们谁也没料到，那个测试其实有多简单。

cues.en: A quick look at the eyes, the hands, and the throat,
cues.zh: 快速扫一眼眼睛、双手和喉咙，

cues.en: and then the writing down their particular details.
cues.zh: 然后登记下个人信息。

cues.en: The point at which many of them lost their old names because the inspectors couldn't spell them, and they couldn't write them. So they became Smith,
cues.zh: 就在这个环节，许多人失去了原来的名字，因为检查员不会拼，他们自己也不会写。于是他们全变成了 Smith，

cues.en: Brown,
cues.zh: Brown，

cues.en: Jones.
cues.zh: Jones。

cues.en: Eight out of ten people passed the test, but with one inspector handling 500 people a day, it was almost a case of, if you could walk, you were in.
cues.zh: 十个人里有八个能通过，但一个检查员每天要看500人，基本只要你还能走，就能通过。

cues.en: In the 30 between 1850 and 1880,
nearly 8,000,000 people got in.
cues.zh: 有近 800 万人涌入。

cues.en: And as the country grew and the frontiers pushed west, the immigrants were swallowed up to disappear in the vast open spaces of this enormous country.
cues.zh: 随着国家扩张、边疆向西推进，这些移民被吞没，消失在这个庞大国家广袤的空旷地带中。

cues.en: The trouble was, every ten years, the government had to find them all again for the national census.
cues.zh: 麻烦在于，每十年政府都得为了全国人口普查把他们重新找出来。

cues.en: And as the population soared, the paperwork for doing that became unbelievable.
cues.zh: 随着人口飙升，这件事的文书工作量变得难以想象。

cues.en: And then in 1880,
cues.zh: 然后到了 1880 年，

cues.en: an army surgeon called John Shaw Billings, who was working on the census, was watching the mountains of paperwork being shuffled when he happened to mention to his young engineer assistant
cues.zh: 一位名叫 John Shaw Billings 的军医当时正参与人口普查，他看着堆积如山的文书被翻来翻去，碰巧对年轻的工程师助手说

cues.en: that he reckoned that the Jaccards
cues.zh: 他认为，那些 Jaccard

cues.en: where they punched holes ought to be able to carry information. You know, if a man was married, you'd punch a hole, and if he wasn't, he wouldn't.
cues.zh: 打孔卡应该能够承载信息。你知道，如果一个人已婚，就打一个孔；如果未婚，就不打。

cues.en: The young engineer, Herman Hollerith, worked on the idea and came up with this.
cues.zh: 这位年轻工程师 Herman Hollerith 研究了这个想法，并做出了这个。

cues.en: It's called a tabulator,
cues.zh: 它叫制表机，

cues.en: and it works on cards like these,
cues.zh: 用的是这样的卡片，

cues.en: the size of a dollar bill of the period. Now Hollerith chose that size because they already had holders for dollar bills, and what that meant was he wouldn't have to design and build one himself.
cues.zh: 大小和当时的一美元纸币一样。Hollerith 选这个尺寸，是因为当时已经有存放美元纸币的盒子；这意味着他不用自己设计制造一个。

cues.en: No fool.
cues.zh: 真不傻。

cues.en: So you put the card in here.
cues.zh: 把卡片放到这里。

cues.en: Now let's say we're talking about a white male, age 35,
cues.zh: 假设我们说的是一个 35 岁的白人男性，

cues.en: who is single, lives in Maine, and came originally from Russia.
cues.zh: 他单身，住在缅因州，原籍俄罗斯。

cues.en: Right. You punch
cues.zh: 好。你打孔：

cues.en: white,
cues.zh: 白人，

cues.en: male,
cues.zh: 男性，

cues.en: single,
cues.zh: 单身，

cues.en: the code for the state,
cues.zh: 州的代码，

cues.en: Maine,
cues.zh: 缅因州，

cues.en: and finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: Russia.
cues.zh: 俄罗斯。

cues.en: Now you take the card out. See the little holes?
cues.zh: 现在把卡片拿出来。看到这些小孔了吗？

cues.en: And put it into this press.
cues.zh: 然后把它放进这台压机。

cues.en: Now, when you push this press down, these little needles here with springs on them either go through a hole
cues.zh: 现在，当你把这台压机压下去，这些带弹簧的小针要么穿过一个孔

cues.en: or they don't.
cues.zh: 要么穿不过去。

cues.en: Remember Jaccard?
cues.zh: 还记得 Jaccard 吗？

cues.en: And if they do go through a hole, they make electrical contact
cues.zh: 如果它们确实穿过孔，就会形成电接触

cues.en: down there.
cues.zh: 就在下面。

cues.en: And that triggers these counters up here one click forward.
cues.zh: 这会让上面的这些计数器咔哒一下往前走一格。

cues.en: Now, depending on what you want to count, you program the counters.
cues.zh: 现在，根据你想统计什么，来设定这些计数器。

cues.en: Say you just want a general population figure. Then all these are the states and territories of which that is Maine, and that one in the corner is the grand total.
cues.zh: 假设你只想要总人口数。那么这些都是各州和各领地，其中这个代表缅因州，角落里那个是总计。

cues.en: So our man in Maine would add one to Maine and one to the grand total like this.
cues.zh: 这样，我们这位在缅因州的人，就会给缅因州加一，再给总计加一，就像这样。

cues.en: And the bell told you, you've done it. Now,
cues.zh: 铃响了就告诉你，完成了。现在，

cues.en: the census involved much more detailed analysis than that. So Hollerith also designed a sorter, this cabinet with lots of boxes in it connected to the tabulator. Now, let's say you want to take a particular look at all 35 year old men. What you do is program the tabulator so that when one of them comes under the press, it causes a particular box to flip open like this.
cues.zh: 人口普查需要比这详细得多的分析。所以 Hollerith 还设计了一台分拣机，就是这个有很多格子的柜子，和制表机相连。现在，假设你想专门看看所有 35 岁男性。你要做的是给制表机设定程序，让其中一个来到压机下时，某个特定的格子像这样弹开。

cues.en: And you pop the card into the box.
cues.zh: 然后你把卡片塞进那个格子。

cues.en: And at the end of the day,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: you took out all the 35 year olds
cues.zh: 你把所有 35 岁的人的卡片取出来

cues.en: and ran them back under the press to see where they all lived and to see how many of them there were. And you could do that with any bit of information on a card or any mixture of bits of information on a card.
cues.zh: 再让它们过一遍压机，看看他们都住在哪里、有多少人。卡片上的任何一项信息，或任意几项信息的组合，你都可以这样统计。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: the 1880 census had taken over seven years to complete.
cues.zh: 1880年人口普查花了七年多才完成。

cues.en: With a new tabulator, the 1890 census was finished in half that time. And they checked the total twice.
cues.zh: 有了新的制表机，1890年人口普查用一半时间就完成了。而且他们把总数核对了两次。

cues.en: Sixty two million nine hundred and forty seven thousand seven hundred and fourteen.
cues.zh: 六千二百九十四万七千七百一十四。

cues.en: So the trail has brought us from the water wheel to the loom,
cues.zh: 于是这条线索把我们水车带到了织布机，

cues.en: and the linen it produced that made paper so cheap it spurred the development of printing,
cues.zh: 以及它产出的亚麻布，让纸张变得如此便宜，从而推动了印刷术的发展，

cues.en: of books that interested people in things like automated organs, whose pegged cylinders gave the French silk weavers the opportunity to run their looms with perforated cards that used to count Americans who had once passed through this hall in Ellis Island.
cues.zh: 书籍让人们开始对自动风琴之类的东西产生兴趣，而自动风琴的带销滚筒又让法国丝织工有机会用穿孔卡来驱动织布机；这些穿孔卡曾被用来统计曾经穿过Ellis Island这个大厅的美国人。

cues.en: Gateway to the one country that more than any other would fall apart if it weren't for Hollerith's card,
cues.zh: 通往这样一个国家：若没有Hollerith's card，它比任何其他国家都更容易分崩离析，

cues.en: used to program the computers without whose help the entire massive structure of the modern world would fall down.
cues.zh: 这些卡被用来给计算机编程，而若没有计算机的帮助，现代世界整个庞大的结构就会倒塌。

cues.en: Most of the ancestors of the computer brought people pleasure.
cues.zh: 计算机的大多数祖先都给人们带来了快乐。

cues.en: What will it bring us?
cues.zh: 它会给我们带来什么？

cues.en: That is precisely the issue that E. G. Marshall and his guests are about to grapple with, and they'll do so in just a moment.
cues.zh: 这正是E. G. Marshall和他的嘉宾即将探讨的问题，他们马上就会开始。
